props.title: City of Angels

sections.content: City of Angels reimagines Wim Wenders' masterpiece Wings of Desire (1987) through a glossy Hollywood lens, trading Berlin's post-war gravitas for sun-drenched Los Angeles. Nicolas Cage plays Seth, an angel who falls for surgeon Maggie (Meg Ryan) in a story that explores the price of mortality and the power of human connection. The film marked a significant shift in supernatural romance, influencing later works like Meet Joe Black (1998) and The Lake House (2006) with its blend of metaphysical themes and earnest love story. sections.content: The late 1990s saw a surge of existential romance films that questioned the boundary between the spiritual and physical worlds. What Dreams May Come (1998) painted a vivid afterlife in pursuit of lost love, while Ghost (1990) had already proven the commercial viability of supernatural romance. These films share DNA with City of Angels in their exploration of love transcending physical boundaries, though each approaches the theme from different angles.

Director Brad Silberling infuses City of Angels with distinctly American optimism, contrasting sharply with Wenders' European art house sensibilities. The film's visual language - angels in black coats perched on LA skyscrapers - created iconic imagery that influenced supernatural cinema for years to come, seen in later works like Constantine (2005) and Legion (2010). sections.content: City of Angels marked a departure from traditional celestial depictions seen in films like It's a Wonderful Life (1946) and Michael (1996). Instead of wings and halos, these angels wore dark suits and observed humanity with detached curiosity. This modern interpretation influenced later works like Dogma (1999) and The Adjustment Bureau (2011), which continued to reimagine divine beings as sophisticated urban observers.
